positive_observations: Fingerprinting retains one 64 KiB buffer, one fixed-size SHA-256 state and a Long byte counter; no whole-file accumulation occurs. Math.addExact rejects overflow.

FileDigest computes from the content URI stream on Dispatchers.IO with runInterruptible. Its concurrently suspended cleanup child cancels the provider CancellationSignal and closes a registered stream when the scope is cancelled; the post-registration interrupt check covers cancellation before stream registration.
Both asset descriptor and input stream have structured use blocks. The result reports observed bytes rather than trusting library metadata.
Hash calculation starts only from the explicit button. A running calculation exposes cancellation, and rememberCoroutineScope is cancelled when the details dialog leaves composition.
Expected fingerprints accept exactly 64 hexadecimal characters after trim and locale-independent normalization. Digest text explicitly uses left-to-right direction.
test_gaps: Existing hash UI coverage checks only a three-byte successful stream and expected-hash comparison. It does not exercise cancellation during descriptor open, cancellation during a blocked read, close-on-cancel, dialog dismissal while hashing, or reopening and recalculating after cancellation. These are coverage gaps, not proven defects.
No bounded-memory large-file/unknown-size or non-zero asset-offset fixture is present in the inspected hash tests.

StreamIntegrity only observes thread interruption. Its OutputStore callers use ordinary withContext rather than runInterruptible; the resulting publication cancellation defect is already covered by reviewer-37 and is not duplicated here.

validation.conclusion: No additional proven defect in the scoped on-demand hashing path.
